general: Make sure that the vehicle you're using can pass a safety inspection. Check that all the lights work (particularly trailer brake lights and turn signals), and that the air brake system is in good condition. Bring appropriate tools.

Know your vehicle: practise the pre-trip inspection. Make sure you can find all the items you'll be inspecting as part of the pre-trip. Have someone watch you conduct the pre-trip inspection and tick off the items you're checking, to make sure you complete everything and can explain what you're doing.

Make sure you're familiar with driving the vehicle you are using for your road test, particularly its handling and turning characteristics and gearshift operation. As part of the road test, you'll be assessed on your ability to shift gears smoothly.
Drive posted speed limits. Don't keep up to speeding traffic. Watch for school zones and playgrounds.
Make full stops for stop signs, and stop in the correct position. When it's safe to move out, pull out slowly, scanning the intersection.
Use the correct traffic lane. Make proper turns as described in this guide.
Mirror check and, if possible, shoulder check whenever you change lanes or direction.
Keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Scan intersections before driving through, even if the light is green when you approach.
Be familiar with commercial vehicle procedures for crossing railway tracks.

knowledgeTestFacts: You need to take knowledge tests whenever you apply for a new licence.
All knowledge tests referred to in this guide are conducted only in English. You must be able to complete these tests without assistance.

The licensing process to obtain a Class 1, 2, 3 or 4 driver's licence, a heavy trailer endorsement, house trailer endorsement or an air brake endorsement is conducted entirely in English. You must be able to communicate in both spoken and written English without assistance.
The knowledge tests are all multiple choice.
The answers to all the knowledge test questions are in this guide.
One of the knowledge tests is a traffic signs test. To prepare, review the signs shown in chapter 11 (signs, signals and road markings) as well as the signs shown in other chapters of the guide.
If you do not qualify on the knowledge test you will need to wait seven days before another attempt can be made.
For road tests, the re-test waiting period is 14 days after a first attempt, 30 days after a second attempt, and 60 days for any subsequent attempts.
A Class 1 road test takes about two hours. Class 2, 3, 4 and heavy trailer endorsement road tests take less than two hours.
All road tests consist of a pre-trip inspection, an air brake pre-trip inspection (if your vehicle is equipped with air brakes), and a road test.

Plan to arrive at the office at least 15 minutes early. You'll have to pay a fee if you don't show up for your scheduled road test and don't provide either 48 hours notice or a valid reason for not attending.
Knowledge and road test fees vary depending on which tests you will be taking; the fees are listed at icbc.com.
An applicant who fails to qualify on the air brake knowledge test after three attempts must complete or repeat an approved 7-hour air brake training course.

The air brake knowledge test results are only valid for one year. Drivers who haven't had the air brake endorsement placed on their driver's licence within one year of passing the air brake knowledge test will need to re-take it.

Every time you go to a driver licensing office, you'll need to take one piece of primary ID and one piece of secondary ID. Photocopies are not accepted (except a photocopy certified as a true copy by the government agency that issued it).
If you hold a higher class out-of-province licence, some tests may be waived; contact your nearest driver licensing office for details.
